items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the parks, recreation and historic preservation law, in relation to the leasing and licensing of property
items.lawSection: Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation Law
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6966

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the parks, recreation and historic preservation law,
in relation to the leasing and licensing of property

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

This bill would authorize the Commissioner of Parks, Recreation and
Historic Preservation to enter into a lease or license not exceed
forty years for the construction of a full service marina and cabins
at Sampson State Park.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of this bill would amend the Parks, Recreation and Historic
Preservation Law (PRHPL) § 3.09(2-d) to add to the list of properties
that the Commissioner may lease or license to a private entity for a
term not to exceed more that forty years, a full service marina and
cabins at Sampson State Park.

Section 2 of this bill would provide that no lease or license entered
into by the Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation for
the marina and cabin construction will result in the impairment of any
existing collective bargaining agreements.

Section 3 of this bill provides for an immediate effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :

PRHPL § 3.09(2-a) authorizes the Commissioner to enter into agreements
for up to twenty years provided that agreements in excess of ten years
provide for a capital investment of no less than one million dollars.
PRHPL § 3.09(2-d) authorizes leases and licenses for specifically
delineated park-related properties for terms of up to forty years, in
recognition that extensive capital improvements to the listed
structures, or new capital construction, require longer-term financial
investment.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New Bill.

 JUSTIFICATION :

OPRHP has a long tradition of working with private entities to invest
in state park facilities to improve the public's experience and
provide necessary resources needed to support park functions. There
has been a growing interest in providing for a new marina at Sampson
State Park and constructing new cabins as well. Private investment is
essential for these projects to succeed and a longer term than twenty
years is needed to attract such a private investor.

Any lease or license will be subject to environmental and historic
preservation reviews, public notice and involvement, and any lease or
license must comply with the State Finance Law. Surrounding park and
historic resources will continue to be protected and any proceeds
realized will be invested in capital improvements to the State Park
system.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :

None

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
